4. Certification & Advisory Services
Auditors are the only professionals authorized to sign off on various official certificates.

Net Worth Certificates: Required for bank loans, visas, or government tenders.

Foreign Exchange Certification (Form 15CA/15CB): Required for remitting money outside India to ensure taxes are paid.

Utilization Certificates: Certifying that government grants or bank loans were spent for their intended purpose.

IPO Advisory: Preparing "Restated Financial Statements" and performing compliance work for companies going public.

Insolvency & Bankruptcy Services: Serving as an Interim Resolution Professional (IRP) in corporate insolvency cases.

3. Specialized & Investigation Audits
These are specific-purpose audits often triggered by events or unique industry requirements.

Forensic Audit: Investigating financial fraud, money laundering, or embezzlement for legal proceedings.

Due Diligence: A thorough financial review conducted before a merger, acquisition, or investment.

Transfer Pricing Audit: Auditing international transactions between related companies to ensure they are at "Arm’s Length Price."

Information Systems (IS) Audit: Reviewing the security and integrity of a company’s IT infrastructure.

RERA Audit: Specific to the real estate sector, ensuring project funds are used as per the Real Estate Regulatory Authority rules.

2. Internal & Management Audits
These are conducted to help management improve operations rather than just to satisfy the law.

Internal Audit: Evaluating the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management, and governance processes.

Operational Audit: Assessing the efficiency of a business's daily operations and identifying "revenue leakages" or waste.

Management Audit: Reviewing the performance of the management team in achieving organizational goals.

In India, a Chartered Accountant (CA) acting as an auditor provides a diverse range of services. These are generally classified into mandatory (statutory) audits, management-led internal reviews, and specialized certifications.

1. Mandatory & Statutory Audits
These are required by specific Indian laws to ensure financial transparency and legal compliance.

Statutory Audit: A mandatory annual audit for all companies (Private or Public) under the Companies Act, 2013, to certify that financial statements show a "true and fair view."

Tax Audit: Conducted under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act for businesses and professionals exceeding specific turnover limits (e.g., ₹1 crore or ₹10 crore).

GST Audit & Reconciliation: While the formal "GST Audit" was replaced by self-certification, CAs are still hired to prepare and reconcile GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C (Annual Return and Reconciliation Statement).

Bank Audit: Specialized audits for banks, including:

Statutory Branch Audit: Annual verification of a bank branch's accounts.

Concurrent Audit: Real-time, daily checking of bank transactions.

Stock & Revenue Audit: Verifying the value of inventory or revenue to ensure loan security.

3. Specialized Audit Services
These address high-stakes or industry-specific needs.

Forensic Audit: Investigating financial fraud, embezzlement, or legal disputes. Often used by banks or in criminal litigation.

RERA Audit: Specific to the real estate sector, ensuring that project funds in "Escrow Accounts" are used correctly as per the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act.

Due Diligence: A thorough financial investigation conducted before mergers, acquisitions, or significant investments.

Information Systems (IS) Audit: Reviewing the security, reliability, and integrity of a company’s IT infrastructure and software.

Transfer Pricing Audit: For companies with international transactions, ensuring they comply with "Arm's Length Price" regulations to prevent tax evasion.

4. Certification & Advisory Services
Auditors are authorized to issue various certificates required by government departments and financial institutions.

Net Worth Certificates: Required for bank loans, visas, or tender applications.

Utilization Certificates: Certifying that government grants or specific project funds were spent as intended.

Project Reports & Feasibility Studies: Helping businesses secure funding by certifying the financial viability of new projects.

IPO Support: Preparing "Restated Financial Statements" and performing the heavy lifting required for SEBI filings during an Initial Public Offering.

In India, the role of an auditor—typically a Chartered Accountant (CA)—is governed by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) and various laws like the Companies Act, 2013, and the Income Tax Act, 1961.

Their services are broadly categorized into mandatory legal requirements, management-led reviews, and specialized investigations.

1. Statutory & Mandatory Audits (Legal Requirements)
These are audits mandated by specific Indian laws to ensure transparency and legal compliance.

Statutory Audit: A mandatory annual review for all companies (Private or Public) under the Companies Act, 2013, to ensure financial statements reflect a "true and fair view."

Tax Audit: Conducted under Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act for businesses and professionals exceeding specific turnover thresholds.

GST Audit/Reconciliation: While formal GST audits by professionals were modified in recent years, auditors still perform GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C reconciliations to align books with tax filings.

Bank Audit: Specialized audits of banking institutions, including Statutory Bank Audits, Concurrent Audits (real-time monitoring), and Stock Audits (verifying collateral for loans).

2. Internal & Management Audits
These are conducted to help management improve operations rather than just to satisfy the law.

Internal Audit: Evaluating the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management, and governance processes.

Operational Audit: Assessing the efficiency of a business's daily operations

owner_posts.post_text:
📢 Income Tax Return Filing Update

Do you know? In certain cases, filing an Income Tax Return (ITR) is important even if your income is within basic exemption limits.

ITR filing may be applicable in cases like:

✅ High value transactions
✅ Foreign assets/income reporting
✅ Business or professional income
✅ TDS/TCS related situations
✅ Other specified conditions under Income Tax rules

File your ITR carefully and keep your financial records updated.

Timely Filing • Better Compliance • Peace of Mind

– All In One Tax Solution

📢 Form 10-IEA – Important Update

Are you opting for the Old Tax Regime while filing ITR-3 or ITR-4?

In certain cases, Form 10-IEA must be filed to exercise the tax regime option. However, ITR-1 and ITR-2 filers generally do not need to file Form 10-IEA, as the tax regime can be selected directly in the Income Tax Return.

Before filing your return, ensure you have selected the correct tax regime and completed the required compliance, wherever applicable.

Stay informed. Stay compliant.

– All In One Tax Solution

📢 GSTR-3B Update | July 2026

From the July 2026 tax period, important changes are being introduced to the GSTR-3B filing process.

Key Highlights:
✅ ITC details will be auto-populated from GSTR-2B.
✅ Manual modification of ITC in GSTR-3B will no longer be available.
✅ Review and reconcile your GSTR-1 and GSTR-2B carefully before filing.
✅ Timely and accurate filing will help avoid compliance issues.

Businesses are advised to verify their GST data before submitting returns.

Stay updated. Stay compliant.

– All In One Tax Solution

📢 GST Update

A proposal for "One Nation, One GST Number" has been discussed as part of ongoing GST reforms.

If implemented in the future, it could help simplify GST registration and compliance for businesses operating across multiple states.

Please note that this is currently a proposal and has not been implemented.

Stay updated with the latest GST developments.

– All In One Tax Solution

📢 ITR Filing Started – AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26)

Income Tax Return filing for AY 2026-27 has begun. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3 and ITR-4 forms are now available for eligible taxpayers.

✔ Salaried Individuals
✔ Capital Gains & Multiple Income Sources
✔ Business & Professional Income
✔ Presumptive Income

"Timely filing today, peace of mind tomorrow."

Stay compliant and file your return on time.

📢 GSTN Update – E-Way Bill Changes

GSTN has extended the implementation date of certain E-Way Bill functionalities from 15 June 2026 to 01 August 2026.

Key Updates:
✅ Mandatory capture of "Ship To GSTIN" in Bill-To / Ship-To transactions
✅ Use of URP where GSTIN is not available
✅ Voluntary Closure of E-Way Bill functionality

Businesses are advised to review their processes and prepare for the upcoming changes.

Effective Date: 01 August 2026
